walkthroughs.body_html:
The Challenge of Resource Management — a core area of GCSE Geography.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

The Challenge of Resource Management brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with The Challenge of Resource Management.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What is the Hubbert curve about?
options: Peak oil
Population
Climate
Migration
Africa
South America
Australia
Central Asia

mcqs.q: What is the difference between constructive and destructive waves?
options: Fold mountains form from giant volcanoes erupting upwards.
Constructive waves have strong swash and weak backwash, building beaches; destructive waves have weak swash and strong backwash, dragging sediment offshore and eroding cliffs.
Big waves are destructive and small waves are constructive.
Constructive waves build sandcastles and destructive waves wash them away.

mcqs.q: Why is the global energy transition slower than many expect?
options: Existing fossil-fuel infrastructure is sunk cost, low-carbon alternatives need vast capital, intermittency requires storage, and political/economic interests resist change — even as costs of renewables fall.
The transition is slow because people don't want to give up cars.
The energy transition is slow because renewable energy doesn't actually work.
Constructive waves build sandcastles and destructive waves wash them away.

mcqs.q: How are fold mountains like the Himalayas formed?
options: By the collision of two continental plates (India and Eurasia) where neither can subduct, so the crust crumples and is forced upwards over millions of years.
Fold mountains form when one plate slides under another into the mantle.
Fold mountains form from giant volcanoes erupting upwards.
Constructive waves build sandcastles and destructive waves wash them away.
